title: Grant Calendar access
intro: Two minutes, sir. One command, one Allow click, and I can see your actual calendar.

steps.title: Why this is needed
steps.body: The morning run reads Calendar.app through a tiny helper app, bin/CalendarHelper.app. It exists because this macOS version refuses to show the permission prompt for plain Terminal scripts (Terminal declares no calendar usage description, so the request dies silently). The helper declares its purpose properly, so macOS lets it ask.
steps.voice: Step one, context. macOS only shows a calendar prompt to a real app that explains itself, so I built one.

steps.title: Run it in Terminal
steps.body: Open Terminal and run the command below. The first run builds the helper if needed, then macOS should ask: CalendarHelper would like full access to your calendar. Click Allow Full Access.
steps.voice: Step two. Run the calendar command in Terminal, and allow full access when CalendarHelper asks.

steps.title: If no prompt appeared
steps.body: A stale denial can be stuck from earlier attempts. Run the reset below, then the step two command again. Still nothing? System Settings, Privacy and Security, Calendars: set CalendarHelper to Full Access, then run step two once more.
steps.voice: Step three, only if the prompt never showed. Reset the permission state and run it again.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Run the check below. status should read ok and today's events list out. The HUD core panel picks them up on the next refresh, and every 7:30 briefing routes the day around real appointments from now on.
steps.voice: Step four. Check the calendar file says status ok. Then we are done, sir.

outro: Calendar sighted. The day plan just got honest.
